# Education in Sweden
Education in Sweden is structured as a comprehensive system beginning with preschool (förskola) for ages 1–6, followed by a mandatory nine-year grundskola (primary school) for ages 6–16. Primary school covers the subjects Swedish, mathematics, English, science, arts, and physical education, and grading begins in year 6, progressing to a letter scale (A–F; E is passing, F fails). After grundskola, students may attend upper secondary school (gymnasieskola), which is elective but has a 99% enrollment rate, and lasts three years. This level offers 18 national programmes, divided into vocational and preparatory tracks, all of which provide basic university admission eligibility. Admission is typically based on grades from the nine-year grundskola, with core subjects required for upper secondary eligibility.
Higher education follows the Bologna Process, offering bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees at universities and university colleges. Admission requires proficiency in Swedish and English, with additional routes via the Swedish Scholastic Aptitude Test (SweSAT). Public universities and university colleges grant a variety of academic and professional degrees, while a separate system provides vocational post-secondary education. Sweden also allows independent (free) schools to operate with public funding, subject to state curriculum requirements; around 10–15% of students attend these schools. The system is noted for its broad access, standardized curriculum, periodic national testing, and financial support for students, with an ongoing debate over the role and regulation of independent, for-profit schools.
